title: Phoenixville mom's story of her daughter's AI chatbot 'friend' reaches the WSJ
summary: Mileva Repasky, a Phoenixville mother and co-founder of the Phone-Free Schools Movement, told The Wall Street Journal how her 12-year-old spent all her screen time confiding in a character-chat bot before Repasky cut off access. The piece cites new research linking AI companionship to loneliness in middle schoolers.

title: Acclaimed organist Carol Williams plays St. John's Lutheran Oct. 11
summary: St. John's Lutheran Church hosts Welsh-born concert organist Carol Williams, San Diego's first woman civic organist and now its civic organist emerita, at 4 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 11. The recital is part of the church's 2026-2027 community concert series.

title: Bridge Street's cat adoption corner holds its grand opening at First Friday
summary: Calla's Kitty Kingdom, a permanent adoption space for Calla's Critter Rescue cats inside the Maddie's Castle pet boutique, marks its official opening with a ribbon cutting from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. Friday, Oct. 2. BarkHop Studio photographs the adoptable cats to help them find homes.

title: Phoenixville Area High School cafeteria cited for running without hot water
summary: A Sept. 25 county inspection found the Aramark-run cafeteria at 1200 Gay St. without building hot water, so staff were boiling water and using temporary boosters at sinks to keep handwashing and sanitizing safe. The water heater was due for repair within three days, with a follow-up inspection to come.

title: Spotlight PA profiles the PACS volunteer who knows every mystery vegetable
summary: Elaine Miller, 72, has volunteered at Phoenixville Area Community Services since 2021 and now sits on its board, helping shoppers try unfamiliar produce with recipes. PACS says it served more than 12,000 people last month as demand keeps climbing.

title: Phoenixville lands nearly $1 million in federal money for firefighter staffing
summary: FEMA awarded the Borough of Phoenixville more than $974,000 through its SAFER program, which pays for firefighter personnel costs plus recruitment and retention. It was among the Mid-Atlantic awards announced Sept. 25.

title: Mapping the license-plate cameras around Phoenixville
summary: Using volunteer-compiled DeFlock data, Patch located known automated license-plate readers nearby: one at Nutt Road and West Bridge Street in the borough, four at Kimberton and Conestoga roads in West Pikeland, and eight in Upper Providence, including the Station Avenue lot by Lowe's. No official count of installations has been published, so the real number is likely higher.
loc: Nutt Road & W. Bridge Street, Phoenixville

title: Alianzas' 16th Cultural Diversity Festival fills Reeves Park Saturday
summary: Alianzas de Phoenixville and People's Light host their annual celebration of the area's immigrant communities from 1 to 5 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 26, with live music and dance, food trucks, family activities, community resource tables and a raffle.

title: Downtown Phoenixville turns into Stars Hollow for a Gilmore Girls weekend
summary: From Sept. 25-27, nine Bridge Street-area shops take on the roles of Gilmore Girls landmarks, with a sticker map and raffle, trivia, karaoke and a Luke and Lorelai look-alike contest at Steel City Coffeehouse.

title: Judy Collins brings her farewell tour to the Colonial in November
summary: The folk singer plays the Colonial Theatre at 8 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20 as part of her farewell tour. Opening is Oakland Rain, a Norwegian indie folk-pop duo of sisters who are longtime Collins collaborators and are touring behind their Twin Flames project.

title: Restored 1859 school bell gets a permanent home in Reeves Park
summary: The borough held a dedication ceremony Tuesday, Sept. 15 for the Church Street School Bell, cast in Sheffield, England in 1859 for Phoenixville's first public school. The bell cracked in 1871 and spent decades inverted as a flower planter before Gern Jeager's crew at Specialty Metals Welding and Fabrication restored it this year.
